## Authentication

The auth collection is **`users`**. The API-key header embeds that slug, and a
wrong slug silently degrades you to the anonymous view instead of failing:

```
Authorization: users API-Key <your key>
```

`pay` builds this header for you from the profile's stored credential. The key
itself is never written to this file, to the audit log, or to any output.
Verify identity with `pay whoami` — a wrong key returns HTTP 200 with a null user.

## Schema discovery

GraphQL answers queries at `/api/graphql`, but **introspection is disabled** (a production
build). Discovery is REST-observed, which degrades:

* field lists come from sampled documents: a field that was `null` there has no type;
* required flags are unknown — `required: null` means unknown, never "optional";
* block slugs and block schemas are not published at all: use the block census
  (`pay blocks types | schema | example | new | validate`, catalog below), not
  `pay describe`, and never the app's source code, to learn block shapes.

To enable it, the app sets `graphQL: { disableIntrospectionInProduction: false }` in
`buildConfig()` and redeploys. `pay doctor` reports the current state.

## Collections (4)

| slug | ops | features | key fields | id |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crm-contacts` | create read update delete | trash folders | `name`, `email`, `status` | number |
| `pages` | create read update delete | drafts versions | `title`, `slug`, `_status` | number |
| `media` | create read update delete | upload folders | `alt`, `filename` | number |
| `payload-migrations` *(internal)* | read | — | `name` | number |

Features decide what is legal: `drafts` means `--draft`/`--published-only` apply,
`versions` means `pay versions` works, `trash` means `pay delete` is a soft delete
and `pay restore` exists, `upload` means `pay upload`/`pay download` work.
Collections marked *(internal)* are Payload's own bookkeeping; they are reachable
but rarely what you want.

A global is a single document: `pay globals get <slug>` and
`pay globals update <slug>`. Updating one is a destructive (L2) operation and
needs `--yes` in a non-interactive shell.

## URLs, draft preview and backups

| | |
|---|---|
| site URL | `http://localhost:3900` (derived:base_url) |
| URL templates | none: `pay url` uses breadcrumbs, else `/{slug}` (a guess outside `pages`) |
| preview route | `/next/preview?path={path}&previewSecret={secret}` (default) |
| preview secret | **not configured**: `pay url --preview` fails with `preview_secret_missing` |
| backups | on: `/work/.pay-backups` (./pay.toml) |

`pay url <collection> <id>` prints a document's site URL; `--preview` mints draft-preview
cookies so a browser shows unpublished drafts (see `references/migration.md` §6).
Every write that changes an existing document saves it first (`meta.backups`);
undo with `pay backups restore <file>`.

## Examples against this project

```bash
pay describe pages --required-only        # what must be set to create one
pay find pages --published-only --limit 5   # never omit --published-only here
pay globals get header --depth 1
pay blocks types pages   # block types per field path, live
pay blocks schema group --collection pages   # what is inside one
```
